message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** representing the thirteen American colonies. These men were chosen by their respective colonial legislatures and served as the official signatories of the document. Here’s a quick overview:

| State | Signers (in order of appearance on the original parchment) |
|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Delaware | Thomas McKean, George Read, Caesar Rodney |
| Pennsylvania | Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, John Morton, George Clymer, James Smith, George Taylor, George Ross, William Allen, John Penn, John Dickinson, George Whitefield, John Penn (the younger), John Penn (the elder) |
| New Jersey | William Livingston, John Witherspoon, Abraham Clark, John Hart, William Livingston (again), John Witherspoon (again) |
| Georgia | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| Connecticut | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, Jonathan Trumbull |
| Massachusetts | John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Joseph Warren, John Hancock (again), John Hancock (again) |
| Maryland | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll (again) |
| South Carolina | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge |
| New Hampshire | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| Virginia | Richard Henry Lee, Francis Lightfoot Lee, Carter Braxton, Thomas Jefferson, George Wythe, James Madison, James Monroe, Edmund Randolph, Thomas Jefferson (again) |
| North Carolina | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn (the younger) |
| Rhode Island | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, William Ellery (again) |

These signers represented a broad spectrum of political views and backgrounds, but all agreed that the colonies should declare independence from Britain. The signing ceremony took place on August 2, 1776, at the Pennsylvania State House (now Independence Hall) in Philadelphia.
